research_question: Can hallucination detectors discriminate supported from minimally incorrect answers while remaining stable across meaning-equivalent answer forms?
gap: Existing work documents label problems, response-length effects, domain shift and detector-family blind spots. The narrower unresolved question is whether factual discrimination survives controlled changes in answer form within the same human-validated items.
contribution: A proposed paired form-invariance audit that evaluates factual discrimination and within-label score stability together under controlled answer transformations.
limitations: The design covers short passage-grounded answers rather than long-form generation with mixed claims.
Meaning-preserving lengthening and minimally incorrect answers require human validation.
A controlled form intervention diagnoses sensitivity but does not prove why a detector uses a feature internally.
unknowns: The datasets, versions, licences, detectors and calibration procedure remain to be frozen.
No proposed experiment has been run and no performance result is established.
The automated paragraph-to-source mappings have not received human approval.
